explanation: Tipping in Spain is a personal reward for good service, not a social obligation — menu prices already include service, and waitstaff don't depend on tips as part of their wage. Most locals round up the bill or leave roughly 5-10% only when service was notably good, and it's more common in sit-down restaurants than bars or cafés. Skipping a tip entirely is not considered rude.
local_tip: Round up to the next few euros or leave about 5-10% for great service; a tip isn't expected for quick coffees or bar drinks.

also_check.note: Tipping can confuse or even offend staff, since excellent service is already the norm and isn't paid for separately.
Tipping 15-20% at restaurants is the norm and servers rely on it as part of their income.
A service charge is built into the bill by law, but rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated.
